district: Maihar (new district created 2023; earlier Satna district)

history.dynasty: Ancient origins; renovated and developed by later rulers and devotees
history.period: Present shrine traditions date to around 502 CE (exact antiquity unverified)
history.summary: Maa Sharda Devi Temple stands atop 600-foot Trikuta Hill at Maihar and is revered as one of the 51 Shakti Peethas — the place where Goddess Sati's necklace (har) fell while Shiva carried her body, giving 'Mai' + 'har' = Maihar ('Mother's Necklace'). The temple is believed to be around 502 CE in origin, though it was renovated by many rulers over time. The hill is reached by 1,063 steps or by ropeway. The temple also has shrines to Ganesh, Kartik Swami and Adi Shankaracharya, and the goddess is depicted as Maha Saraswati holding a book and a pot of honey. The medieval warrior Alha (of Alha-Udal fame) is legended to have worshipped here daily; Alha Talaab (tank) survives nearby. Note: sources list Satna district, but Maihar became a separate district in 2023. Coordinates approximate (hilltop site).

name: Maa Sharda Devi Temple
town_description: Maihar is a town in the Vindhya region of Madhya Pradesh, famous for the Maa Sharda Devi Temple on Trikuta Hill, a major Shakti Peetha. It is the home of the Maihar gharana of Hindustani classical music founded by Ustad Allauddin Khan. The town is also an industrial centre with large cement factories in the surrounding area.

travel.airport: Jabalpur (Dumna) Airport ~140 km (verify); Prayagraj Airport ~155 km (verify)
travel.road: Trikuta Hill, ~5 km from Maihar town/railway station; ropeway available for those unable to climb the 1,063 steps

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Navratri is the peak festival
visitor_information.opening_hours: Darshan 5:00 AM–8:00 AM and 4:00 PM–9:00 PM; aartis 5:00 AM, 1:00 PM, 7:00 PM; ropeway 7:00 AM–1:00 PM and 1:30 PM–7:00 PM (timings may vary — verify)
